ru: не ложиться спать (дожидаясь кого-л.); дожидаться, дождаться
separable: no object — intransitive; the person you are waiting for follows *for*: *wait up for me*.
gloss: To stay awake instead of going to bed until someone comes home.
examples: Don't *wait up* — I'll be back after midnight.
She *waited up* until two in the morning.
His parents were still *waiting up* when he got in.

separable: no object — intransitive, and it is usually an imperative shouted at someone ahead of you: *wait up!*
gloss: To stop or slow down so that a person behind you can catch up.
examples: *Wait up!* I can't walk that fast in these shoes.
He *waited up* at the top of the trail.
The guide kept *waiting up* for the slower hikers.

separable: separable — *wait out the storm*, *wait the storm out*, and a pronoun must split it: *wait it out*, never ✗ *wait out it*.
gloss: To stay where you are until something unpleasant is over.
examples: We *waited out* the rain under a gas station awning.
Sometimes there is nothing to do but *wait* it *out*.
They're *waiting out* the worst of the heat indoors.

ru: ждать без дела, прождать; торчать в ожидании
separable: no object — intransitive; what you are waiting for follows *for*: *wait around for a callback*.
gloss: To stay somewhere doing nothing while you wait for something to happen.
examples: I'm not going to *wait around* all day for the plumber.
We *waited around* for an hour and then left.
She's tired of *waiting around* for an answer.

ru: уходить, уйти (демонстративно); покидать, покинуть в знак протеста
separable: no object — intransitive; the place follows *of*: *walk out of the meeting*.
gloss: To leave a place suddenly to show that you are angry or offended.
examples: He *walked out* in the middle of the argument.
Half the audience *walks out* before the second act.
She has *walked out* of two jobs this year.

ru: объявлять забастовку, забастовать; прекращать, прекратить работу
separable: no object — intransitive: *the drivers walked out*. The noun is one word: *a walkout*.
gloss: (Of workers) to stop working as a protest.
examples: The nurses *walked out* on Monday morning.
Three thousand drivers are *walking out* at midnight.
They have *walked out* twice in five years.

separable: inseparable — *walk out on your family*, never ✗ *walk your family out on*.
gloss: To abandon someone or something that depends on you.
examples: Her father *walked out on* them when she was six.
You can't just *walk out on* a signed contract.
He's *walking out on* the band right before the tour.

ru: разгуливать, разгулять (обед, боль); сгонять, согнать ходьбой
separable: separable — *walk off the calories*, *walk the calories off*; with a pronoun it must split: *walk it off*, which is also what a coach yells at a player who has just been hit.
gloss: To get rid of a pain, a bad mood, or a heavy meal by going for a walk.
examples: We *walked off* Thanksgiving dinner around the block.
He's outside *walking off* a bad mood.
The trainer told her to *walk* it *off* and get back in.

ru: легко выигрывать, выиграть; получать, получить без труда
separable: inseparable — the prize follows *with*: *walked off with first prize*, never ✗ *walked first prize off with*.
gloss: To win something easily.
examples: Their documentary *walked off with* four awards.
She *walks off with* the science prize every single year.
He has *walked off with* the title three seasons running.

separable: inseparable — *walk off with my umbrella*, never ✗ *walk my umbrella off with*.
gloss: To take something that belongs to someone else and leave with it.
examples: Somebody *walked off with* my umbrella.
Two men *walked off with* a laptop in broad daylight.
People keep *walking off with* the good pens.

separable: inseparable — what you abandon follows *from*: *walk away from the deal*. With no object, plain *walk away* means the same thing.
gloss: To decide to stop being involved in something difficult and leave it behind.
examples: They *walked away from* the deal at the last minute.
You can't *walk away from* a mortgage that easily.
She *walked away from* a twenty-year career and never looked back.

separable: inseparable — *walk in on a meeting*, never ✗ *walk a meeting in on*.
gloss: To enter a room and accidentally interrupt something private.
examples: I *walked in on* them arguing about money.
She's terrified of *walking in on* her boss again.
He *walks in on* every conversation without knocking.

ru: объяснять шаг за шагом, объяснить; проводить, провести по всем этапам
separable: the person always goes in the middle — *walk me through it*, *walk the client through the contract*; ✗ *walk through me*. The noun is one word: *a walkthrough*.
gloss: To explain something to someone slowly, one step at a time.
examples: Can you *walk* me *through* the setup?
She *walked* the jury *through* the timeline twice.
He's *walking* the new hire *through* the checklist.

ru: брать назад (слова), взять назад; отступать, отступить от сказанного
separable: separable — *walk back the statement*, *walk the statement back*, *walk it back*. Very common in American news writing.
gloss: To take back or soften something you said publicly.
examples: The mayor *walked back* his comments the next morning.
They spent a week *walking* it *back*.
She has *walked back* that promise twice already.

separable: no object — intransitive: *the dog wandered off*.
gloss: To leave a place slowly and without telling anyone, usually getting lost.
examples: The toddler *wandered off* in the store.
Don't *wander off* — the bus leaves in ten minutes.
Two of the goats have *wandered off* again.

separable: separable — *ward off a cold*, *ward the mosquitoes off*, *ward it off*.
gloss: To keep something harmful or unwanted away from you.
examples: She takes zinc to *ward off* colds.
The smoke *warded off* the mosquitoes for about an hour.
The company is *warding off* a takeover with a lawsuit.

separable: separable — *warm up the soup*, *warm the soup up*, *warm it up*.
gloss: To heat food, a room, or an engine that has gone cold.
examples: *Warm up* the leftovers in the oven, not the microwave.
He *warmed up* a plate of rice at midnight.
She's *warming* the car *up* in the driveway.

separable: no object in this sense — intransitive: *the team warmed up for twenty minutes*. With an object it means preparing an audience: *warm up the crowd*.
gloss: To do gentle exercise to get your body ready for harder activity.
examples: Always *warm up* before you run.
They *warmed up* for half an hour before the match.
The band is *warming up* backstage.

ru: проникаться симпатией, проникнуться; привыкать, привыкнуть (к кому-л.)
separable: inseparable — *warm up to the idea*, never ✗ *warm the idea up to*.
gloss: To gradually start to like someone or something you were unsure about.
examples: It took her months to *warm up to* the new manager.
I'm slowly *warming up to* the idea of moving.
He never really *warmed up to* living in the city.

separable: separable — *warm over the same speech*, *warm it over*. The adjective is even commoner: *a warmed-over policy*.
gloss: To present old ideas or old material again as if they were new.
examples: The candidate just *warmed over* his speech from 2018.
They keep *warming over* the same three proposals.
The report has been *warmed over* so many times that nobody reads it.

separable: no object — intransitive: *go wash up before dinner*.
gloss: To wash your hands and face, especially before a meal.
examples: Go *wash up* — dinner is on the table.
He *washed up* at the kitchen sink.
The kids are *washing up* now.
contrast: A real US/UK trap: American *wash up* means wash your hands, British *wash up* means do the dishes. Note the *-es* in the third person: *he washes up*.

ru: прибиваться к берегу, прибиться; выбрасываться, выброситься на берег
separable: no object — intransitive, and the place follows *on*: *washed up on the beach*.
gloss: (Of something in the water) to be carried onto the shore.
examples: A whale *washed up* near the pier last weekend.
Bottles *wash up* here after every storm.
Debris has been *washing up* for two weeks.
contrast: The participle became an adjective: a *washed-up* actor is one whose career is over.

separable: separable when it has an object — *wash off the mud*, *wash it off* — and it also works with no object: *the paint washed off in one rinse*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*wash the dye off*), intransitive (*it washed off easily*)
gloss: To remove something from a surface with water, or to come off when washed.
examples: *Wash off* the sunscreen before you get in the pool.
The marker *washed off* the table right away.
She's *washing* the paint *off* her hands.

ru: срывать из-за дождя, сорвать; отменять, отменить из-за непогоды
separable: separable, though it is usually passive — *the game was washed out*; the active *the rain washed out the picnic* is fine too.
gloss: (Of rain) to make an outdoor event impossible, so that it is canceled.
examples: Rain *washed out* the second game of the series.
The parade has been *washed out* twice in three years.
Storms are *washing out* half the weekend schedule.

ru: не выдерживать отбора, не выдержать; отсеиваться, отсеяться
separable: no object — intransitive, and the program follows *of*: *washed out of flight school*. The noun is one word: *a washout*.
gloss: To fail a difficult training program and have to leave it.
examples: He *washed out* of the academy in the first month.
About a third of the class *washes out* before spring.
Two recruits have already *washed out*.

separable: separable — *wash down the pills*, *wash them down*; the drink follows *with*: *wash it down with water*.
gloss: To drink something in order to swallow food or medicine more easily.
examples: He *washed down* the pills with orange juice.
*Wash* it *down* with plenty of water.
They were *washing down* burgers with cheap beer.

separable: separable — *wash down the walls*, *wash the walls down*, *wash them down*.
gloss: To clean a large surface by covering it with water.
examples: They *wash down* the trucks every Friday.
He *washed down* the deck with a hose.
The crew is *washing* the boat *down* before the inspection.

separable: separable — *wash away the topsoil*, *wash it away*; it also works with no object: *the footprints washed away*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*the flood washed away the bridge*), intransitive (*the chalk washed away*)
gloss: To carry something off or destroy it with moving water.
examples: The flood *washed away* two bridges.
Rain has *washed away* all the chalk drawings.
The tide is slowly *washing* the sandbar *away*.

separable: inseparable — *relief washed over her*, never ✗ *washed her over*; the person always follows the particle.
gloss: (Of a strong feeling) to come over someone suddenly and completely.
examples: Relief *washed over* her when the call finally came.
A wave of exhaustion *washes over* me every afternoon.
Panic was *washing over* the whole room.

separable: no object — intransitive: *he wasted away in the hospital*.
gloss: To become thinner and weaker over a long period, usually from illness.
examples: He *wasted away* over the last year of his illness.
The cattle were *wasting away* in the drought.
She has *wasted away* to almost nothing.

separable: no object at all — intransitive, and most often a shouted warning: *watch out!*
gloss: To be careful because there is danger.
examples: *Watch out!* That branch is about to come down.
He wasn't *watching out* and walked straight into a pole.
You'd better *watch out* — she remembers everything.
contrast: *watch* takes *-es* in the third person: *she watches out*.

separable: inseparable — *watch out for potholes*, never ✗ *watch potholes out for*.
gloss: To stay alert for something dangerous, or for something you are hoping to see.
examples: *Watch out for* deer on this stretch of road.
We *watched out for* his car all afternoon.
You have to *watch out for* hidden fees with that airline.

separable: inseparable — *watch over the children*, never ✗ *watch the children over*.
gloss: To look after someone or something in order to keep them safe.
examples: A neighbor *watches over* the house while they travel.
She *watched over* him all night after the surgery.
Two rangers were *watching over* the campsite.

separable: separable — *water down the paint*, *water the juice down*, *water it down*.
gloss: To make a drink or another liquid weaker by adding water to it.
examples: That bar *waters down* the well drinks.
He *watered down* the juice for the kids.
They've been *watering* it *down* for years and nobody noticed.

separable: separable — *water down the bill*, *water it down*; the participle is everywhere as an adjective: *a watered-down version*.
gloss: To make a rule or a proposal less strong so that fewer people object to it.
examples: The Senate *watered down* the bill until it did almost nothing.
Every draft gets *watered down* a little more.
They're *watering down* the safety rules again.

separable: separable — *wave off the suggestion*, *wave it off*, *wave him off*.
gloss: To refuse or dismiss something with a small gesture, as if brushing it aside.
examples: He *waved off* the apology and changed the subject.
She *waves* every compliment *off*.
The offer was *waved off* without any discussion.

separable: separable — *wave down a cab*, *wave the driver down*, *wave it down*.
gloss: To signal to a driver to stop by waving your arm.
examples: We *waved down* a cab on Ninth Avenue.
He stood in the road *waving down* traffic.
A ranger *waved* us *down* at the gate.

separable: inseparable — *weasel out of the deal*, never ✗ *weasel the deal out of*. Informal, and always disapproving.
gloss: To avoid a duty or a promise by being dishonest or clever.
examples: He *weaseled out of* paying his half of the bill.
She's trying to *weasel out of* the contract.
They have *weaseled out of* every commitment so far.
contrast: American English keeps one *l*: *weaseled*, *weaseling*; British English doubles it.

separable: separable — *weed out the weak applications*, *weed the duplicates out*, *weed them out*.
gloss: To remove from a group the people or things that are not good enough.
examples: The first interview *weeds out* half the candidates.
They *weeded out* the duplicate records overnight.
We're *weeding* the bad data *out* this week.

ru: высказываться, высказаться; вмешиваться, вмешаться в обсуждение
separable: no object — intransitive; the topic follows *on*: *weigh in on the budget*.
gloss: To join a discussion and give your opinion, usually with some authority.
examples: The governor *weighed in* on the school closures.
Everybody *weighs in* and nothing ever gets decided.
Two economists have *weighed in* since Friday.
contrast: *weigh* keeps its silent *gh* in every form: *weighs*, *weighed*, *weighing*.

separable: no object — intransitive; the weight follows *at*: *weighed in at 180 pounds*. The noun is one word: *the weigh-in*.
gloss: (Of an athlete) to be weighed officially before a competition.
examples: Both fighters *weigh in* tomorrow at noon.
He *weighed in* at 147 pounds.
She has *weighed in* under the limit every single time.

separable: separable — *weigh down the branches*, *weigh them down*; very common in the passive: *weighed down with groceries*.
gloss: To make something heavy so that it bends or moves slowly, or to burden someone with worry.
examples: Wet snow *weighed down* the power lines.
She was *weighed down* with two bags and a stroller.
Student debt is *weighing* them *down*.

separable: inseparable — *the decision weighs on him*, never ✗ *weighs him on*. Often *weigh on someone's mind*.
gloss: (Of a worry or a decision) to trouble someone continuously.
examples: The decision *weighed on* her for months.
It *weighs on* him every single night.
Money worries have been *weighing on* the whole family.

separable: no object — intransitive: *tears welled up*.
gloss: (Of tears or a strong feeling) to rise up suddenly.
examples: Tears *welled up* before she could finish the sentence.
Anger *wells up* every time he tells that story.
You could feel the pride *welling up* in the whole room.

separable: separable — *while away the afternoon*, *while the hours away*, *while it away*. Slightly literary.
gloss: To pass time in a pleasant, unhurried way.
examples: They *whiled away* the whole afternoon on the porch.
He *whiles away* the winter reading detective novels.
We *whiled* the layover *away* in an airport bookstore.
contrast: The verb is *while*, not *wile* — *wile away* is a very old misspelling that some dictionaries now list as a variant, but *while away* is the safe spelling.

ru: быстро готовить, приготовить (на скорую руку); состряпать
separable: separable — *whip up a salad*, *whip something up*, *whip it up*.
gloss: To make a meal or something else quickly and without much effort.
examples: She *whipped up* an omelet in about five minutes.
I can *whip* something *up* for lunch if you're hungry.
He's *whipping up* a batch of pancakes for everyone.
contrast: *whip* doubles its *p* before an ending: *whipped up*, *whipping up*.

separable: separable — *whip up support*, *whip it up*, though the noun usually stays after the particle.
gloss: To deliberately excite a strong feeling in a group of people.
examples: The speech *whipped up* the crowd in about a minute.
They're *whipping up* opposition to the new tax.
Real anger has been *whipped up* over a rumor.

separable: separable — *whip out a phone*, *whip it out*.
gloss: To pull something out quickly and suddenly.
examples: He *whipped out* his phone and started recording.
She *whips* her badge *out* before anyone can ask.
They were *whipping out* credit cards all night.

ru: быстро справляться, справиться (с чем-л.); проскакивать, проскочить
separable: inseparable — *whip through the paperwork*, never ✗ *whip the paperwork through*.
gloss: To finish a task or get through material very quickly.
examples: She *whipped through* the paperwork in under an hour.
He *whips through* a novel a week.
We were *whipping through* the checklist until the printer jammed.

separable: separable — *whisk away the plates*, *whisk them away*; very often passive: *she was whisked away to the hospital*.
gloss: To take someone or something away quickly and suddenly.
examples: A waiter *whisked away* the empty plates before we finished.
He was *whisked away* by security.
They're *whisking* her *away* to the airport right now.

separable: separable — *whittle down the list*, *whittle it down*; the target follows *to*: *whittled down to three*.
gloss: To reduce something gradually until only a small part is left.
examples: They *whittled down* four hundred applicants to six.
The debt has been *whittled down* to almost nothing.
We're *whittling* the list *down* this week.

ru: трусить, струсить; идти, пойти на попятную
separable: no object — intransitive; what you backed out of follows *of*: *wimped out of the race*. Informal.
gloss: To decide at the last minute that you are too afraid to do something.
examples: He *wimped out* right before the jump.
Don't *wimp out* on me now.
She's *wimping out* of the presentation again.

ru: уничтожать, уничтожить; стирать, стереть с лица земли
separable: separable — *wipe out the colony*, *wipe it out*; commonly passive: *the village was wiped out*.
gloss: To destroy something completely so that nothing is left.
examples: The late frost *wiped out* the whole crop.
One bad quarter *wiped out* forty years of savings.
The disease is *wiping out* the bee population.

separable: separable, and with a pronoun it must split — *that trip wiped me out*, never ✗ *wiped out me*. Usually passive: *I'm wiped out*.
gloss: To make someone extremely tired.
examples: The red-eye *wiped* me *out* for two days.
Two hours of yard work *wipes* him *out*.
She's completely *wiped out* after a week of night shifts.

separable: no object — intransitive: *he wiped out on the last turn*. The noun is one word: *a wipeout*.
gloss: To fall off or crash while surfing, skiing, or riding.
examples: He *wiped out* on the last turn and lost the lead.
She *wipes out* every time she tries that trick.
Two riders have already *wiped out* on the wet corner.

separable: separable — *wipe down the counter*, *wipe the table down*, *wipe it down*.
gloss: To clean a surface by rubbing it with a damp cloth.
examples: *Wipe down* the counters before you leave.
He *wiped down* every table twice.
She's *wiping* the shelves *down* right now.

separable: separable — *wipe off the crumbs*, *wipe them off*, and the surface can follow: *wipe the crumbs off the table*.
gloss: To remove something from a surface by rubbing it.
examples: *Wipe off* the counter, please.
He *wiped* the dust *off* the screen with his sleeve.
Most of the fingerprints have been *wiped off*.

separable: separable — *wipe up the spill*, *wipe it up*; it also works with no object: *somebody wipe up in aisle four*.
gloss: To clean up a spilled liquid with a cloth or a towel.
examples: Somebody *wipe up* that juice before it gets sticky.
He *wiped up* the spill with a dish towel.
She's still *wiping up* after the party.

separable: separable — *wipe away the tears*, *wipe them away*.
gloss: To remove tears or marks with your hand or a cloth.
examples: He *wiped away* a tear and kept reading.
She *wipes* the condensation *away* every morning.
Twenty years have not *wiped away* the memory.

ru: умнеть, поумнеть; браться, взяться за ум
separable: no object — intransitive, often an imperative: *wise up!* What you finally understand follows *to*: *wise up to the scam*. Informal.
gloss: To finally understand the truth about a situation and stop being fooled.
examples: *Wise up* — they are never going to promote you.
Customers *wised up* fast once the fees appeared.
He's finally *wising up* to how the place works.

separable: separable — *wolf down a sandwich*, *wolf it down*.
gloss: To eat something very fast and greedily.
examples: He *wolfed down* two sandwiches before practice.
She *wolfs* her lunch *down* at her desk.
They were *wolfing down* pizza when I walked in.
contrast: As a verb *wolf* is regular and keeps the *f*: *wolfs down*, never ✗ *wolves down* — *wolves* is only the plural noun.

ru: хотеть выйти (из дела); желать уйти, порвать
separable: inseparable, and *of* names the thing: *want out of the deal*. Informal but very common in American speech.
gloss: To want to leave a job, a deal, or a relationship.
examples: He *wants out* of the lease.
She *wanted out* of the marriage years before she said so.
Two partners have *wanted out* since the audit.

ru: хотеть участвовать; хотеть войти в дело
separable: inseparable, and *on* names the thing: *want in on the deal*. Informal.
gloss: To want to join something that other people are already doing.
examples: Everybody *wants in* on the new fund.
He *wanted in* from the very first meeting.
She keeps saying she doesn't *want in*, and then she shows up.

separable: separable — *wall off the section*, *wall it off*; commonly passive: *the unit is walled off from the rest of the company*.
gloss: To separate something completely from everything around it.
examples: The company *walled off* the research team from sales.
That part of his life has been *walled off* for years.
They're *walling* the old wing *off* during construction.

separable: no object — intransitive: *work out three times a week*. The noun is one word: *a workout*.
gloss: To exercise in order to get stronger or fitter.
examples: She *works out* before work every morning.
He *worked out* for an hour and could barely walk afterward.
They've been *working out* together since January.

ru: решать, решить; вычислять, вычислить; разбираться, разобраться
separable: separable — *work out the answer*, *work the answer out*, *work it out*.
gloss: To find the answer to a problem by thinking about it or calculating it.
examples: I can't *work out* how they got that number.
She *worked out* the total in her head.
We're still *working* the schedule *out*.

separable: no object — intransitive: *it all worked out*. An adverb often follows: *worked out great*.
gloss: To end well, or to happen in a particular way in the end.
examples: Don't worry — this kind of thing usually *works out*.
The move *worked out* better than anyone expected.
Things have *worked out* fine for both of them.

separable: separable — *work out a deal*, *work the details out*, *work it out*; the other side follows *with*: *work it out with the landlord*.
gloss: To reach an agreement, or to arrange the details of something.
examples: The two sides *worked out* a deal over the weekend.
We're *working out* the payment schedule now.
They have *worked out* who covers which shift.

ru: составлять, составить (в итоге); выходить, выйти (о сумме)
separable: inseparable — *it works out to twelve dollars each*, never ✗ *works twelve dollars out to*.
gloss: To add up to a particular amount when you calculate it.
examples: With tip, it *works out to* about twelve dollars a person.
The raise *worked out to* less than a dollar an hour.
After fees their offer has *worked out to* almost nothing.

separable: separable — *work up an appetite*, *work up the nerve*, *work it up*.
gloss: To develop something in yourself gradually, through effort.
examples: We *worked up* a real appetite on the hike.
He finally *worked up* the nerve to ask her.
She's *working up* a serious case against the company.

separable: separable, and it splits with a pronoun — *don't work yourself up*, ✗ *work up yourself*. The participle is a common adjective: *all worked up*.
gloss: To make someone become very upset or excited.
examples: Don't *work* yourself *up* over a rumor.
The crowd was already *worked up* before he said a word.
Sugar *works* the kids *up* every single time.

ru: подходить постепенно, подойти (к чему-л.); доводить, довести до (постепенно)
separable: inseparable — *work up to a marathon*, never ✗ *work a marathon up to*.
gloss: To move gradually toward something bigger or harder.
examples: Start with two miles and *work up to* ten.
He *worked up to* asking for a raise over about a month.
She's *working up to* telling them she's leaving.

separable: separable — *work off the debt*, *work the calories off*, *work it off*.
gloss: To get rid of a debt, extra weight, or a bad mood by working or exercising.
examples: He *worked off* the loan in two years.
She goes running to *work off* stress.
They're out in the yard *working* dinner *off*.

separable: inseparable — *work through the grief*, *work through the list*; never ✗ *work the list through*.
gloss: To deal with a difficult problem or feeling step by step until it is resolved.
examples: It took a year to *work through* the grief.
They *worked through* every objection on the list.
He's still *working through* what happened last spring.

separable: inseparable — *work around the problem*, never ✗ *work the problem around*. The noun is one word: *a workaround*.
gloss: To find a way to deal with a problem without actually removing it.
examples: We *worked around* the missing data and filed anyway.
The whole team *works around* his schedule.
They're *working around* a broken oven all weekend.

ru: втискивать, втиснуть (в расписание); включать, включить (между делом)
separable: separable — *work in a few jokes*, *work them in* — and with a person it splits: *can you work me in at three?*
gloss: To fit something or someone into a schedule or a text that is already full.
examples: The dentist can *work* you *in* at four.
He *worked in* two jokes about the budget.
She's *working* a nap *in* before the red-eye.

separable: separable when it has an object — *wrap up the meeting*, *wrap it up* — and it also stands alone: *let's wrap up*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*wrap up the discussion*), intransitive (*we wrapped up around six*)
gloss: To bring something to an end.
examples: Let's *wrap up* — we're out of time.
They *wrapped up* the meeting in twenty minutes.
Filming has *wrapped up* early for once.
contrast: *wrap* has a silent *w* and doubles its *p*: *wrapped up*, *wrapping up*.

separable: usually reflexive or with no object at all — *wrap up warm*, *wrap yourself up*, *wrap the kids up*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*wrap the baby up*), intransitive (*wrap up, it's freezing*)
gloss: To put warm clothes on, or to put them on someone else.
examples: *Wrap up* — it's twenty degrees out there.
She *wrapped* the baby *up* in two blankets.
They came in *wrapped up* in scarves and hats.

separable: separable — *wrap up the gifts*, *wrap the leftovers up*, *wrap them up*.
gloss: To cover something in paper or plastic, especially as a present.
examples: I still have to *wrap up* the presents.
He *wrapped up* the leftovers and put them in the fridge.
She's *wrapping* everything *up* in old newspaper.

ru: биться над (чем-л.), ломать голову; мучиться, помучиться
separable: inseparable — *wrestle with a decision*, never ✗ *wrestle a decision with*.
gloss: To struggle for a long time with a difficult problem or decision.
examples: He *wrestled with* the decision for weeks.
She's still *wrestling with* the ending of the book.
The committee has *wrestled with* this question since March.
contrast: Silent *w* and silent *t*: *wrestle* is said RES-ul.

separable: inseparable — *wriggle out of the chore*, never ✗ *wriggle the chore out of*. Americans say *wiggle out of* just as often.
gloss: To avoid doing something you are supposed to do, by making excuses.
examples: He *wriggled out of* jury duty somehow.
She's always *wriggling out of* doing the dishes.
You are not going to *wriggle out of* this one.

separable: separable — *yell out an answer*, *yell it out* — and it also works with no object: *she yelled out in pain*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*yell out a number*), intransitive (*he yelled out when he saw us*)
gloss: To say something suddenly in a very loud voice.
examples: Somebody *yelled out* the wrong answer.
*Yell* it *out* if you see him in the crowd.
She was *yelling out* directions from the porch.

separable: inseparable — *zero in on the problem*, never ✗ *zero the problem in on*.
gloss: To direct all of your attention to one particular thing.
examples: Investigators *zeroed in on* a single supplier.
She *zeroes in on* the weak spot in any argument.
They're *zeroing in on* a release date.
contrast: The third-person form is spelled *zeroes* or *zeros*; *zeroes in on* is the commoner choice.

separable: separable — *zip up your jacket*, *zip the bag up*, *zip it up*.
gloss: To close something with a zipper.
examples: *Zip up* your coat — it's freezing.
He *zipped up* the tent and went to sleep.
She's *zipping* the duffel *up* now.

separable: inseparable — *zip through the chapters*, never ✗ *zip the chapters through*.
gloss: To get through something very quickly.
examples: He *zipped through* the first three chapters in a night.
We *zip through* this part of the course every year.
She was *zipping through* the forms until one wouldn't scan.

separable: fixed — the object is always *it* and nothing else can go there: ✗ *zip your mouth*. Nearly always an imperative, and rude to a stranger.
transitivity: transitive — but only with the fixed object *it*
gloss: To stop talking.
examples: *Zip it* — she's about to announce the winner.
He *zipped it* the second his boss walked in.
Those two would not *zip it* through the entire movie.

separable: no object — intransitive: *I zoned out halfway through*. Informal.
gloss: To stop paying attention and let your mind go blank.
examples: I *zoned out* halfway through the lecture.
He *zones out* whenever the topic is money.
She was *zoning out* at her desk by three o'clock.

separable: no object — intransitive: *he zonked out on the couch*. Informal.
gloss: To fall asleep very quickly because you are exhausted.
examples: He *zonked out* before the movie even started.
The kids *zonk out* in the car every time.
She's been *zonking out* right after dinner all week.

separable: no object of its own — intransitive; the target follows *on*: *zoom in on the license plate*.
gloss: To make the image on a screen or in a camera look closer and bigger.
examples: *Zoom in* on the license plate.
She *zoomed in* until the text was readable.
He's *zooming in* too far to see the whole chart.

separable: no object — intransitive: *zoom out a little*.
gloss: To make an image look smaller so that you can see more of it.
examples: *Zoom out* — I can't tell where that is.
He *zoomed out* to show the whole coastline.
The map keeps *zooming out* on its own.
